📌 Key Takeaways

Section-by-Section Study Breakdown

9.1 Expected Learning Outcomes

  • Establishes essential concepts, mathematical or computational foundations, and techniques of expected learning outcomes.
  • Applies standard methodologies relevant to modern data science workflows and analysis in mining big data.

9.2 Finding Similar Items

  • Establishes essential concepts, mathematical or computational foundations, and techniques of finding similar items.
  • Applies standard methodologies relevant to modern data science workflows and analysis in mining big data.

9.3 Finding Similar Sets

  • Jaccard Similarity of Sets Jaccard similarity is defined in the context of sets.
  • Consider two sets – set A and set B, then the Jaccard similarity JSA,B is defined as a ratio of the cardinality of the set A∩B and cardinality of the set A∪B.
  • It can be used to identify a collection of almost similar documents, news items, web pages or reports.
  • This is also referred to as the character- level similarity of documents.

9.3.1 Jaccard Similarity of Sets

  • Jaccard similarity is defined in the context of sets.
  • Consider two sets – set A and set B, then the Jaccard similarity JSA,B is defined as a ratio of the cardinality of the set A∩B and cardinality of the set A∪B.
  • It can be used to identify a collection of almost similar documents, news items, web pages or reports.
  • This is also referred to as the character- level similarity of documents.

9.3.2 Documents Similarity

  • Finding document similarity is an interesting domain of use of Jaccard similarity.
  • It can be used to identify a collection of almost similar documents, news items, web pages or reports.
  • This is also referred to as the character- level similarity of documents.
  • Another kind of document similarity also looks at documents having similar meanings.

9.3.3 Collaborative Filtering and Set Similarity

  • In the past decade, e-commerce has gained acceptance by customers.
  • Many of you, who have purchased and have liked various items on these e-commerce websites, get online recommendations for the purchase of certain items.
  • You may have observed that many times those recommendations are very close to purchases that you would like to do in the near future.
  • Similarity of the sets is used to address this problem.

9.4 Finding Similar Documents

  • In the last section, we discussed the Jaccard similarity in the context of sets.
  • We also explained the issues of document similarity.
  • The document similarity can be checked using the following process: Step 1: Create Sets of items from the document (Shingles are used) Step 2: Perform Minhashing and create documents Signatures that can be tested for similarity checking.
  • This reduces the number of shingles to be tested for checking the similarity of two documents.

9.4.1 Shingles

  • In order to define the term shingle, let us first try to answer the question: How to represent a document as a set of items so that you can find lexicographically similar documents?
  • One way would be to identify words in the document.
  • However, the identification of words itself is a time-consuming problem and would be more useful if you are trying to find the semantics of sentences.
  • One of the simplest and efficient ways would be to divide the document into smaller substrings of characters, say of size 3 to 7.
